summary: multisample_pid.py likelihood truncated a --label-column value with int() before checking it, so a label other than 0 or 1 between -1 and 2 (for example 0.7) was counted as background or signal with status ok instead of being refused.

observables: likelihood curve: efficiency, misid, rejection and their intervals
impact.bias: events whose label lay in (-1, 0) or (0, 1) were counted as background and those in (1, 2) as signal, changing the curve's efficiency, misid and rejection (one event labelled 0.7 beside one signal and one background event: misid 1/2 instead of a rejection), with status ok and no warning
impact.trigger: multisample_pid.py likelihood with --label-column whose column holds a value other than 0 or 1 strictly between -1 and 2

outputs.how_to_recognize: JSON on stdout of multisample_pid.py likelihood with a curve; the output does not show the labels: check the label column of the input events file for values other than 0 and 1; no artifact records the run

remedy: check the label column of the input; fix the labels to 0 or 1 and rerun (a version with the fix refuses the file and names the value)
